steps.text: Combine salt, vinegar, and water in a large pot, and bring to a boil over high heat.
Add eggs one at a time, being careful not to crack them. Reduce the heat to a gentle boil, and cook for 14 minutes.
Once eggs have cooked, remove them from the hot water, and place into a container of ice water or cold, running water. Cool completely, about 15 minutes. Store in the refrigerator up to 1 week.

raw_recipe.headline: Perfect Hard-Boiled Eggs
raw_recipe.description: Get perfect hard boiled eggs every time with this foolproof recipe that uses a little salt and vinegar to help make hard boiled eggs easier to peel.

video.description: In this video, we'll show you a foolproof method for cooking hard boiled eggs. The eggs are cooked to perfection in boiled water that's been stirred together with vinegar and salt. The result is a perfectly yellow yolk and a tender white.
video.name: Ken's Perfect Hard Boiled Egg

review.reviewBody: This recipe does actually produce "Perfect Hard Boiled Eggs"! My husband loves hard boiled eggs and quite frankly so do I and nothing is more frustrating than something so simple turning out improper or down right ugly when doing deviled eggs or wanting something pretty to garnish a nice salad. I let the eggs come to room temp. to reduce cracking. When adding the eggs to the water I use a slotted spoon and gently place them into the pot this also helps to remove them. These were very easy to peel and the yolk has a nice rich yellow color. Thanks Ken!

Thanks for all of those that have posted comments to my receipe. I heard alot of discussion about eggs cracking when you put them into the boiling water. So, I did what every husband would do..ask the wife! Her trick as indicated in some of the reviews, is to allow them to become room tempeture before going into the water. Seems to work perfect everytime. Once again, thanks to all that have posted and have a Happy Easter.

Brilliant, Ken! I've always used salt (supposed to prevent the contents leaking out) but the vinegar is news, and it works! 14 minutes is a bit long, I think; 10 minutes total boiling time will produce a less rubbery white and a creamy yolk, if you plunge the eggs into cold water immediately. Also crack the shells immediately after putting the eggs in cold water. This will allow the gas to escape which turns the yolk blue.

Wow! I've been cooking for over 50 years and finally today I made perfect boiled eggs for deviling. Have tried everything anybody told me from poking holes in the ends with a needle/fingers to vinegar in the water to standing on my head. This recipe really works. My eggs were extra large so I boiled them the full 15 minutes but a couple extra minutes would have been better. I would have had soft-boiled if I had taken the advise of one reviewer and only boiled for 10 minutes. Like most of the other reviewers I recommend following the recipe exactly. Thanks Ken...wish I had discovered this recipe years ago. Who knew you would need a recipe for boiled eggs...ha ha!!!

For those who had their eggs crack after carefully lowering them into the boiling water? It's because the ice cold eggs are hitting boiling water. Allow the eggs to get to room temp and this recipe works perfectly. And use cool water to cool them down, not ice water...again, it's the super hot hitting the super cold that will cause the shell to crack. Also, if you're making Deviled eggs and want the yolk perfectly centered in the middle of the egg, GENTLY stir the eggs for about 2 or 3 minutes after placing them in the boiling water.

Super simple & PERFECT! I did use red wine vinegar because I was out of the white... couldn't taste it & it gave the egg shells a light pink tint so I could store them with the unboiled & know the difference!

I've boiled eggs this way for many, many years with one exception...which will guarantee no "grey" ring that you get from the sulfur...I put the eggs in the salted/vinegar water before bringing to a boil - uncovered. Once It's boiling, cover pot w/ lid and turn off heat. Leave on burner for 15-20 min. depending on how many eggs. Drain water and soak in ice cold water for 10 min.

Here is the DEFINITIVE way to make hard boiled eggs. It will change your life. Use a double boiler (or even a vegetable steamer inside of a pot). Put water in the pot up to the bottom of the double boiler or steamer. Bring to a boil. Put the eggs in the double boiler or steamer, put the cover on the pot, and continue to boil for exactly 11 minutes. No need to immerse in ice but you can run them under cold water if you want to eat right away. Believe me these eggs can be peeled so easily as you get your finger under the thin membrane that covers the white of the egg. This is foolproof. I have been doing it for many years.s No vinegar, nothing added to the water.

This used to be my go to method for hard boiled eggs and it works reasonably well. Now I use a pressure cooker 5-5 method and find it even better. Add eggs and one cup water. Pressure cook on high 5 minutes then slow release for 5 minutes. Do a quick release and put in ice water. Perfect peel every time. Rare cracked egg.

It's a waste of salt & vinegar and 14 minutes is way too long. The correct way to boil eggs that peel perfectly is: 1. Bring water to boil 2. Drop eggs into water and boil for 12 minutes 3. Drop boiled eggs into ice bath 4. Let cool for 5 minutes then peel. Perfect every time.

This recipe might be ok, but I have eaten hard boiled eggs at least once a week for years with no difficulty peeling them. I put the eggs in a pot of cold water. Turn the burner on high. When I hear them boiling I turn down the burner to a low boil and set the timer for 9 minutes. When done I run them under cold water until warm to the touch. I crack them on the counter and start peeling making sure to get under the skin. If the skin should be stubborn I run more cold water between the egg and the skin. Eggs come out perfect every time.
Perfectly done, easily peeled. Use this method all the time now.
Simple recipe, easy to make, eggs turned out good.

That was probably the worst experience peeling eggs I've ever had. I used eggs from my neighbor's chickens, plus vinegar, plus baking soda, and still got mush after 15 minutes of cooking and cooling. Thank goodness I'm only making potato salad!

As a chef in the college cafeteria the only change is to put the eggs in the steamer. This is equivalent to putting them in BOILING water. Necessary when doing ten dozen eggs at a time. After cooling, EVERY one shelled perfectly. Now that's amazing !!!

I didn’t use the vinegar. I just brought the water to a boil in a deep pot, carefully added the eggs, one at a time. Covered the pot and let it boil for 15 minutes. Then emptied the hot water from the pot and ran cold water over the eggs. then added ice and let eggs sit in the ice water for at least 15 to 20 minutes. The eggs peeled beautifully. I had been using the method where you put the eggs in cold water and brought the eggs to a boil, turned off after boiling, covered the pot and left the eggs sit in the hot water for 15 minutes. Peeling the eggs using that method was a horror. The shells just almost refused to come off. Using the boiling water first recipe makes peeling the eggs super easy. They literally roll off the egg.
All I had available was white wine vinegar but the eggs turned out perfect! I will definitely use this recipe from now on! Thanks Ken!
Perfect every time!
I have always had a problem getting the perfect hard-boiled egg. This was very easy and every egg was perfect!
Took me no time at all, no issues. I ALWAYS have problems doing Hard Boiled Eggs. This worked GREAT! I did peel 1 to make sure it peeled good and it did!
